title: Chronometric Rollout Hub — time-phased rollout visualizer + rollback simulator
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:

This ticket scopes a mid-fidelity prototype for a "Chronometric Rollout Hub": a single-pane console view that emphasizes time-phased rollout state, a live chronometer for active ramps, and an integrated rollback simulator that predicts user-facing impact and cost delta for reversal actions. The design balances operational speed (fast rollback with a single action) with contextual decisioning (signal overlays, dependency map, and estimated cost/latency consequences).

Goals:
- Surface how long each cohort has been at current exposure and time-to-next-step (chronometer + projected timeline).
- Provide a deterministic rollback simulator that shows: expected traffic rebalancing, short-term latency/cost change, and confidence interval on errors prevented.
- Make rollback and pause actions discoverable but guarded by a lightweight briefing that lists reason signals and suggested mitigation.
- Visualize upstream/downstream dependencies (routes, feature flags, and model variants) so operators understand blast radius before executing safety actions.
- Support both canary and A/B scenarios and make multi-variant rollbacks straightforward (revert one variant without affecting others).

Scope and constraints:
- No backend implementation in this ticket; prototype integrates with synthetic telemetry (latency, error-rate, quality-regression metric) and mock dependency graph for validation.
- Will explore an in-console simulation engine UI — does not run production traffic replays.
- Interactions must fit current Console chrome and follow Redwood token standards (spacing/typography/colors).

Key flows included in prototype:
1) Start-of-canary: author sets a time-phased ramp (e.g., 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 72h). Hub shows chronometer for active cohort and projected next step with ETA.
2) Auto-signal pause: when a threshold is hit, a modal/briefing appears with required signal list (what tripped), impact preview, and primary rollback button.
3) Rollback simulator: before confirming, operator sees a side-by-side projection (current vs. rollback) for traffic split, expected tokens-per-second cost delta, and a 95% CI for error reduction based on historical heuristics.
4) Dependency inspection: clicking "blast radius" overlays a dependency map and flags linked routes and private deployments potentially affected.
5) Can I revert single variant?: select variant and the UI simulates reverting only that variant and shows remaining active variants and their projected exposures.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- How much data do we surface by default vs. on demand? We prefer quick glance metrics with a "drill-open" panel for details.
- Simulator accuracy vs. complexity: initial version will prioritize interpretable heuristics over complex ML prediction to avoid misleading numbers.
- Autosave vs explicit confirm for rollback: we recommend explicit confirm with optional "fast rollback" setting in org preferences.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype demonstrates all key flows in clickable Figma with at least two telemetry scenarios (gradual increase in latency, sudden quality regression).
- Designer handoff assets include component variants for chronometer, timeline slider, dependency overlay, and rollback briefing microcopy.
- Usability notes from 3 quick internal reviews recorded in comments.
- Product/Eng alignment: list of 3 minimal backend APIs required for MVP (time remaining, simulated rollout projection, dependency fetch) documented in comments/attachments.

Deliverables:
- Figma prototype link (mid-fidelity clickable)
- Annotated screenshots for developer handoff
- Draft copy for rollback briefing and safety confirmations
- A short demo script (3–4 min) for PM/Eng review sessions

UX principles applied:
- Time-first: operators think in elapsed time; chronometer reduces ambiguity about how long a cohort has been under observation.
- Safeguarded immediacy: enable fast action with clear, reversible paths and a simulator that builds confidence.
- Minimal cognitive load: collapse advanced details behind progressive disclosure while keeping critical signals in one glance.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Clickable Figma prototype covering flows: start canary, auto-pause briefing, rollback simulator, dependency overlay; 2) Handoff assets for components used in prototype; 3) 3 internal review notes addressed; 4) PM and ENG signoff on minimal backend APIs.
